title: Get warnings, call for help and stay in touch
intro: Readings on how official warnings reach you, what to say when you call for help, and how to stay informed when the phones, the internet or the power are down.

limits.text: In a power cut, or when the mobile network fails, many warning channels stop working.
Take official warnings seriously: they tell you how to protect yourself and others.
If the emergency numbers do not work, go to the nearest police station or hospital, if you can.
If a message fails any of the checks, do not pass it on.
In a blackout, do not jam the phone lines looking for news: listen to the radio and call only for emergencies.
